previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic abdominal pain, and migraines was admitted for acute on chronic anemia discovered during a routine exam. She had recently undergone g-tube removal and reported increasing fatigue and migraine frequency. Initial evaluation revealed a hemoglobin of 7.6 g/dL, prompting a blood transfusion. Imaging showed no acute bleed, but an endoscopy identified a bleeding arteriovenous malformation in the mid-jejunum, which was successfully cauterized. She received IV iron and had her PPI dose increased. Her hemoglobin improved to 9.2 g/dL by discharge. Migraine-related stuttering and twitching occurred but resolved spontaneously. Hypoglycemia was managed with dextrose-containing fluids. She was discharged home with stable vital signs, instructions to monitor for GI bleed symptoms, and follow-up labs to track her hemoglobin.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

Thank you for letting us participate in your care. You were 
admitted to the hospital here at ___ because you were 
experiencing worsening abdominal pain and fatigue. Your 
hemoglobin was found to be low, which we felt was contributing 
to your fatigue. We gave you an iron transfusion, and you noted 
improvement. We also performed a colonoscopy to identify 
possible sources of GI bleeding. We found ulcers in your rectum 
and duodenum, which should not cause significant bleeding but 
were biopsied.

We also got imaging of your abdomen to evaluate your abdominal 
pain. The radiology findings were consistent with your chronic 
condition and not an obstruction. It was not felt that you 
needed surgery or a G tube at this time.

Your chronic anemia should be followed-up as an outpatient, as 
you may need regular IV iron infusions. You will also need 
ongoing outpatient follow-up with your gastroenterologist and 
psychiatrist.

Sincerely,
Your ___ Care Team
